arxiv-2201-02014.title: Effective Action, Spectrum and First Law of Wedge Holography
arxiv-2201-02014.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the effective action, the mass spectrum and the first law of entanglement entropy for a novel doubly holographic model called wedge holography. We work out the effective action of quantum gravity on the branes. In the perturbative formulation, it is given by an infinite sum of Pauli-Fierz actions.

arxiv-2201-09172.title: An Attention-based ConvLSTM Autoencoder with Dynamic Thresholding for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Multivariate Time Series
arxiv-2201-09172.creator: Tareq Tayeh 1, Sulaiman Aburakhia 1, Ryan Myers 2, Abdallah Shami 1
arxiv-2201-09172.description: Abstract As a substantial amount of multivariate time series data is being produced by the complex systems in Smart Manufacturing (SM), improved anomaly detection frameworks are needed to reduce the operational risks and the monitoring burden placed on the system operators.

arxiv-2208-13808.title: A discretization of Holst’s action for general relativity
arxiv-2208-13808.creator: Carlos E. Beltrán 1,2, José A. Zapata 1
arxiv-2208-13808.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Carlos E. Beltrán 1,2, José A. Zapata 1. We present a simplicial model for gravity written in terms of a discretized Lorentz connection and a discretized tetrad field. The continuum limit of its action is Holst’s action for general relativity. With the intention of using it to construct spin foam modes for quantum gravity, we write two other equivalent models written in terms of a discretized and constrained B B field.

arxiv-2210-12017.title: Fast dispersion tailoring of multi-mode photonic crystal resonators
arxiv-2210-12017.creator: Francesco Rinaldo Talenti 1,2,∗ , Stefan Wabnitz 1,3 , Inès Ghorbel 2 , Sylvain Combrié 2 , Luca Aimone-Giggio 2 , Alfredo De Rossi 2
arxiv-2210-12017.description: Abstract We introduce a numerical procedure which permits to drastically accelerate the design of multimode photonic crystal resonators. Specifically, we demonstrate that the optical response of an important class of such nanoscale structures is reproduced accurately by a simple, one-dimensional model, within the entire spectral range of interest. This model can describe a variety of tapered photonic crystal structures.

arxiv-2304-07224.title: Unusual Low-Energy Collective Charge Excitations in High- T c T_{c} Cuprate Superconductors
arxiv-2304-07224.creator: Vyacheslav M. Silkin, Stefan-Ludwig Drechsler, Dmitry V. Efremov
arxiv-2304-07224.description: Abstract Despite decades of intensive experimental and theoretical efforts, the physics of cuprate high-temperature superconductors in general, and, in particular, their normal state, is still under debate. Here, we report our investigation of low-energy charge excitations in the normal state.

arxiv-2504-16354.title: VeriFix: Verifying Your Fix Towards An Atomicity Violation PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2504-16354.creator: Zhuang Li, Qiuping Yi, Jeff Huang
arxiv-2504-16354.description: Abstract Atomicity violation is one of the most serious types of bugs in concurrent programs. Synchronizations are commonly used to enforce atomicity. However, it is very challenging to place synchronizations correctly and sufficiently due to complex thread interactions and large input space. This paper presents VeriFix , a new approach for verifying atomicity violation fixes.

arxiv-2510-06811.title: BlackboxNLP-2025 MIB Shared Task: Exploring Ensemble Strategies for Circuit Localization Methods
arxiv-2510-06811.creator: Philipp Mondorf, Mingyang Wang, Sebastian Gerstner, Ahmad Dawar Hakimi
arxiv-2510-06811.description: Abstract The Circuit Localization track of the Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark (MIB) evaluates methods for localizing circuits within large language models (LLMs), i.e., subnetworks responsible for specific task behaviors. In this work, we investigate whether ensembling two or more circuit localization methods can improve performance. We explore two variants: parallel and sequential ensembling.

pmc-10606231.title: Deep Learning-Based Approaches for Enhanced Diagnosis and Comprehensive Understanding of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
pmc-10606231.creator: Marwa Elseddik, Khaled Alnowaiser, Reham R. Mostafa, Ahmed Elashry, Nora El-Rashidy, Shimaa Elgamal, Ahmed Aboelfetouh, Hazem El-Bakry
pmc-10606231.description: Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a prevalent medical condition resulting from compression of the median nerve in the hand, often caused by overuse or age-related factors. In this study, a total of 160 patients participated, including 80 individuals with CTS presenting varying levels of severity across different age groups.

pmc-11657724.title: Cumulative incidence and treatment effectiveness of low bone mineral density among people living with HIV in Iran (2021–2023)
pmc-11657724.creator: Hamidreza Rashidi, Soheil Mehmandoost, Noushin Fahimfar, Seyed Mohammad Hosseinian, Mohammad Reza Shakibi, Tarlan Hasan Aghaei, Farzaneh Yazdi Yahaabadi, Pouriya Salajegheh, Willi Mcfarland, Afshin Ostovar, Hamid Sharifi
pmc-11657724.description: BackgroundThe introduction of antiretroviral therapy (ART) has significantly improved the life expectancy of people living with HIV (PLHIV), leading to an increased prevalence of age-related comorbidities such as osteoporosis. This study investigates the incidence and characteristics of low bone mineral density (BMD) and the treatment effectiveness of low BMD participants among PLHIV in Kerman, Iran.

pmc-12438494.title: Are negative symptoms evaluated with a self-assessment tool or a semi-structured interview more strongly correlated to mental health-related quality of life?
pmc-12438494.creator: J. Montvidas, E. Zauka, Ž. Žumbakys, V. Adomaitienė
pmc-12438494.description: IntroductionNegative symptoms are one of the core symptom groups of schizophrenia. These symptoms are highly prevalent and are proven to have a strong correlation with mental health-related quality of life. Evaluating negative symptoms using the Brief Negative Symptoms Score (BNSS), a semi-structured interview, is recommended. BNSS can be supplemented with the Self-assessment of Negative Symptoms (SNS), a self-assessment scale.

pmc-12514275.creator: Chao Wu, Danwei Shen, Binwei Qin, Jiayan Deng, Haigang Hu, Xiangyu Wang, Lian Xu, Hong Li, Taicong Yang
pmc-12514275.description: exploring the therapeutic efficacy of a 3D-printed multiple microporous titanium metatarsal and polyethylene sesamoid prosthesis based on finite element analysis. A patient with defect in the first metatarsal was enrolled. A digital model of the first metatarsal and medial cuneus prosthesis was designed from the contralateral images and the relevant anatomical parameters measured in the preoperative period (Model A).

pmc-12741114.title: The interaction of regulated forms of cell death in the pathogenesis of severe facial paralysis and potential therapeutic strategies
pmc-12741114.creator: Xing Tang, Ziqin Ji, Xueling Xiao, Tongtong Zhu, Shoujen Lan, Yeayin Yen, Xin Shao, Shune Tan, Chao Wang, Jicheng Zhang
pmc-12741114.description: Neuronal cell death plays a central role in the pathogenesis of facial paralysis. In the constructed severe facial paralysis model, axonal damage becomes the key factor triggering retrograde neuronal degeneration, resulting in a large number of neuronal deaths, which seriously affects the function of the facial nerve.

pmc-12931872.title: Limited Clinical Benefit of the Subacromial Balloon Spacer in Massive Irreparable Rotator Cuff Tears
pmc-12931872.creator: Waleed Albishi, Mishari Alanezi, Noura Alnasser, Khalid Murrad, Emad Elansary, Abdulrahman Alaseem
pmc-12931872.description: »Subacromial balloon spacer (SBS) implantation has been proposed as a minimally invasive treatment for massive irreparable rotator cuff tears (MIRCTs), particularly in elderly patients with preserved glenohumeral articulation and limited functional demands.»Across observational studies, SBS has been associated with short to midterm improvements in pain and shoulder function, reflected by increases in ASES and Constant-Murley scores.

pmc-13261882.title: Puberty-Associated Emergence of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
pmc-13261882.creator: Gil Mashiah, Nili Schamroth, Gili Yaeger-Yarom, Livia Kapusta, Alexander Lowenthal
pmc-13261882.description: BackgroundHypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetically heterogeneous disease with variable and incomplete penetrance, with phenotypic expression occurring across developmental stages, potentially influenced by hormonal and other biological modifiers. Genotype-positive individuals may remain phenotype-negative during childhood, with phenotypic expression emerging during adolescence or early adulthood. Factors influencing the timing of phenotypic conversion remain incompletely understood.
